memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Let me get you something to eat, so you can be refreshed and then go on your way - now that you have come to your servant." "Very well," they answered, "do as you say." So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said, "get three seahs of the finest flour and knead it and bake some bread." - Gen 18:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the gap between what Abraham promised and what he provided. He offered "something to eat" - a modest bite. But then he springs into action: three seahs of the finest flour (an enormous amount of bread), and as we'll see, a whole tender calf. He promised a little and gave a feast. This is generosity that overdelivers.

There is a lovely principle here: Abraham said little and did much. So often we are the opposite - we promise grandly and deliver poorly, or we make a show of our giving. Abraham quietly understated what he would do, then lavished his guests with far more than he had led them to expect.

Notice too the flurry of activity - "quick," "hurried," everyone set to work. Real generosity is not passive or reluctant; it is energetic, glad, wholehearted. Abraham didn't sigh and grudgingly find some scraps. He threw himself into blessing his guests.

This is the spirit God loves. "God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Cor 9:7). And it reflects God's own character, for He is the God who gives "immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine" (Eph 3:20). Our God always overdelivers. When we give generously and gladly - promising little and giving much - we reflect the extravagant heart of the God who gave us His own Son. Let your generosity exceed people's expectations today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to overpromise and underdeliver, or the reverse?
- Is your giving reluctant, or glad and wholehearted?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, make me generous like Abraham - quick to serve, glad to give, offering more than expected. Thank You that You always overdeliver in Your grace. Let my generosity reflect Your extravagant heart.
Amen.
